metadata.title: Claude, Action Creator.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether a Claude Skill is code Claude runs or a file it reads, using the action-creator skill as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that a Skill is a folder of fixed steps, not new intelligence — the button does exactly what's written, every time, and nothing that isn't.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (the one-click payment-reminder button: reliable on repeat clicks, silent on anything outside the file)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes a Skill must be code Claude runs. It isn't — a Skill is a file of instructions Claude reads before it acts. So what's actually inside one?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'A Skill must be some code Claude runs automatically. Is that it?', hesitates on 'code', corrects to 'file', lands the real question

props.text:
A Skill must be
some code Claude
runs automatically.
Is that it?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('code' -> 'file') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Open the folder and there's no program to run — just a SKILL.md file, plain text, and a templates folder beside it. Two files. This one is action-creator. Claude reads SKILL.md before it acts; the file is the instruction set, not a script running somewhere behind it.

shot.new_visual_element: The two-file folder: SKILL.md called out as plain text, templates folder beside it, no executable in sight

production_viz.label: A folder, not a program
production_viz.mechanic: A folder icon opens on cream to reveal exactly two items: a SKILL.md document (marked 'plain text') and a templates folder. No executable, no compiled icon anywhere. A label reads 'action-creator'. The SKILL.md is called out with a line: 'the instruction set.'

beats.narration_text: Inside SKILL.md is a Steps section, and Claude works through it top to bottom — read the request, run the step, return the result. Ask for a one-click button that sends a payment reminder to a specific vendor, and action-creator turns that into a saved action: click it once, and the same email goes out, every time you press it.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — Steps executed top to bottom, then a saved one-click payment-reminder button appears and is clicked

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — read, run, return, then a saved button
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Three phases stack top to bottom and light in sequence: 'Read the request', 'Run the step', 'Return the result'. Below, a one-click button labelled 'Send payment reminder' appears, gets clicked once, and an envelope icon flies out. THIS EXACT BUTTON RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: That's why the button is reliable — the steps in the file don't change between clicks, so the same request produces the same email every time. But ask that same button to negotiate the invoice instead of just sending it, and nothing happens beyond what's already there — negotiating was never written into the file. The skill only does what the page in front of it says.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same button clicked three times identically, then asked to negotiate and going nowhere

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — reliable, then out of scope
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 BUTTON RETURNS, identical. It is clicked three times; each click sends the same envelope, marked teal 'same result'. Then a new label appears beside it — 'negotiate the invoice' — with an arrow to the button that goes nowhere, struck through in terracotta, beside the words 'not in the file'.

beats.narration_text: A Skill isn't new intelligence — it's a folder of fixed steps Claude reads before acting, so a one-click button does exactly what's written, every time, and nothing that isn't.

props.quote: A Skill isn't new intelligence — it's a folder of fixed steps Claude reads before acting, so a one-click button does exactly what's written, every time, and nothing that isn't.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. I want a one-click action that archives newsletters from a specific sender. Read the action-creator skill and walk me through what you'll do before you do it — show me each step in order, so I can see exactly what the button will run. Liam, in for Bear.
